newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Profit-taking deflates Brussels bourse, UCB weighs.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking deflates Brussels bourse, UCB weighs.

text.p: Sliding shares in chemical and drugs firm UCB, the declining dollar and some light profit-taking in only moderate volume kept the Brussels bourse in the red on Thursday, shunning buoyancy in other markets.

But traders said the underlying mood remained positive, and they expected the market to move up again after a brief pause to catch its breath -- although views were mixed on how brief the pause would be.
"We hope the market will move up again. We do not see this as the start of a sell-off," one trader said. "This is pure profit-taking."
"We feel that the market is going up again, although we hope it will go down," another trader said. "We hope that the market will consolidate during the summer."

Traders said the main depressing influence on the market on Thursday was the decline in UCB shares following its revelation late on Wednesday that pre-tax current profits rose 33 percent in the first half of the year -- in line with expectations.
"This was a case of buying the expectations and then selling the fact," one trader said.
"Some people expected UCB to pull something extra out of its hat, and were disappointed when it didn't," another said.
UCB shares, which have a weighting of nearly 12 percent in the blue-chip Bel-20 stock index, ended 3.4 percent down at 134,500 francs after at one stage dropping to 133,100 francs.
But traders also noted that UCB was an illiquid stock and therefore the down move had been somewhat exaggerated.
Indeed, they said, the whole day had been relatively thinly traded, a fact that served to exaggerate the general decline.
The Bel-20 index closed 0.66 percent lower at 2,579.30.
Dollar sensitives were among the losers, notably steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, cement maker CBR and electronics firm Barco.
The market had also been waiting for oil major PetroFina and chemical group Solvay to report their first half figures.
After the market closed PetroFina reported a 61 percent jump in net profit to 10.8 billion francs -- slightly ahead of expectations.
Solvay, on the other hand, was broadly in line with expectations with a slight rise in net current profit to 6.1 billion francs.
